input: A gravity settler is used to remove activated sludge from a process stream, and the sizing of the unit is based on a design overflow rate of 1.67 m h-1 at a throughput of 233 m3 h-1, from which a plan area of 140 m2 is obtained for the settler. The relationship between these figures is a straightforward one, since dividing the throughput of 233 m3 h-1 by the overflow rate of 1.67 m h-1 gives the plan area of 140 m2 that the design adopts. It is worth noting, however, that the overflow-rate basis on which the whole sizing rests is a vendor rule for this solid, and that no settling test on the actual slurry has been run, so the design figures have not been confirmed against the behaviour of the material that the settler will in fact receive. The design procedure that has been followed is the conventional one for a unit of this kind: a permissible overflow rate is selected for the solid in question, the throughput that the unit is required to handle is established, and the plan area is then obtained directly from those two quantities, the intention being that a settler of that area will pass the required flow without exceeding the rate at which the solid can be expected to separate.
target:
A gravity settler removes activated sludge from a process stream. Design overflow rate is 1.67 m h-1 at a throughput of 233 m3 h-1, giving a plan area of 140 m2.

The overflow rate is the throughput divided by the plan area: the flow the settler accepts per unit of settling surface. The plan area follows from the two design figures (233 m3 h-1 divided by 1.67 m h-1 gives 140 m2), and it is the area the stated flow requires if the overflow rate is not to be exceeded. A larger throughput at the same area would raise the overflow rate above the design value, and the sizing holds only while the design rate is kept.

The overflow rate is the design handle on the settler. At the design rate, the upward velocity of the liquid in the settler is the rate at which a particle must settle to be removed, and the area is chosen so that the throughput does not drive that velocity higher. A larger throughput on the same area would raise the overflow rate beyond the design value, and the sizing would no longer rest on the vendor's rule.

The overflow-rate basis is a vendor rule for this solid. No settling test on the actual slurry has been run, so the rate the design assumes is the vendor's figure for the solid class, not a measured property of the slurry the settler will receive.
